CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who reports injuring his right elbow approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He was throwing a ball when the pain started. He reports being hit several times with a lacrosse stick by his 13-year-old son and may have been struck in the elbow area. He describes the pain as sharp and radiating down the forearm, occurring with any movement of the elbow. He denies falling. He took ibuprofen for a couple of days and reports it provided some relief. X-ray obtained prior to visit shows no fracture or bony abnormality.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain and abdominal pain. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart exam reveals a grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur, known from prior.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension, diabetes, systolic ejection murmur.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 500 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient plays lacrosse with his children, ages 13 and 10. Follows a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake at home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right elbow exam shows pain to palpation of the olecranon area of the posterior elbow, mild pain with flexion and extension, and normal range of motion. Mild swelling and bruising noted. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart with grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur.

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: no fracture, no bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right elbow contusion from blunt trauma. Plan: ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily, ice three times daily for 20 minutes, avoid lacrosse for the next couple of weeks to allow healing. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily for hypertension. Continue metformin 500 mg daily for diabetes. Obtain A1C to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment needed in the future.
